title: Provable deletion and auditability for derived analytics artifacts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When users request deletion of PII from the analytics pipeline (e.g., event-level user identifiers, email hashes, or prompt text), downstream derived artifacts remain: time-series aggregates, embeddings, cached feature vectors, sampled exports used for dashboards, and anonymized cohorts. Current deletion workflows focus on raw event pruning but do not provide a verifiable audit that derived artifacts were removed or expired. This creates regulatory and customer risk (GDPR/CCPA requests, enterprise contracts) and undermines trust.

Goal: Implement a provable deletion workflow and audit trail for derived analytics artifacts such that when an identity-linked deletion request is processed we can:
- Identify and expire or scrub all derived artifacts (aggregates, embeddings, caches, feature stores, exported snapshots) that materially depend on the removed PII.
- Emit a tamper-evident audit record listing artifacts examined, actions taken, and cryptographic hashes for snapshot state before/after deletion where feasible.
- Provide an API and Console UI surface for compliance teams to lookup deletion proofs per request ID.

Scope: This ticket covers backend services and pipelines in Console analytics (storage, ETL, feature store, and export pipelines). It excludes UI polish and Dedicated/private deployment packaging which will be separate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Given a validated deletion request, the system enumerates downstream artifacts potentially influenced by the identity within a bounded time window and produces an actions plan
Artifacts identified are either expired (time-based tombstone), scrubbed (redacted or nullified fields), or re-aggregated to remove contribution from deleted identities according to policy

A cryptographic audit record is generated and stored in an immutable ledger (append-only blob with SHA256 fingerprints) containing request metadata, enumeration results, actions taken, and pointers to affected storage locations
Console and Compliance APIs can retrieve the deletion record by request ID and show status: Pending, In Progress, Completed, Failed with error details
End-to-end tests simulate deletion of synthetic PII and assert that embeddings/feature-store rows with the identity are removed or marked expired and that derived aggregates are updated within SLA
Security review completed and design meets internal compliance checklist
Performance: typical deletion of a single-identity footprint (<=10k events) completes enumeration and action plan within 2 minutes and pipeline remediation within 30 minutes for non-archived data
tech_notes:
Design overview:
1) Lineage-first enumeration: Leverage existing event lineage metadata (event->derived-feature mapping) to fast-path artifact discovery. For artifacts lacking explicit lineage, use a best-effort bloom-filter index built per-day that maps identity-hashed tokens to storage buckets.
2) Action types: expire (set TTL/tombstone), scrub (field-level redact), re-aggregate (rerun aggregate excluding identity contributions), and delete (remove object). For embeddings/feature-store rows, prefer expire+scrub to preserve index stability when full recompute is prohibitively expensive.
3) Audit record: JSON envelope with request_id, requester, timestamp, enumeration snapshot (list of object URIs), actions planned, actions applied, pre/post SHA256 hashes for small objects (<=64KB). Large blobs reference chunk-level hashes. Write audit records to an append-only S3 prefix with object immutability policy and also replicate hash digests to the compliance Postgres store for fast lookup.
4) Verification: Post-action verification job computes post-action fingerprints and compares against expected state; any mismatch flags the request for manual review.
5) Backfill strategy: For historical data older than retention window, include a sampling + extrapolation policy and surface residual risk in the audit record.
6) Idempotency: Assign a canonical deletion request UUID; replaying the same request should be safe and produce the same final state or a no-op with a linked audit record.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Full recompute vs. expirations: full recompute ensures zero residual contribution but is expensive for high-cardinality aggregates. We'll default to recompute for aggregates with cardinality < threshold, otherwise expiration with documented risk.
- Bloom-filter false positives: will increase enumeration noise but not miss artifacts. Need to tune false-positive rate and monitor overhead.
- Cryptographic proofs vs. legal sufficiency: hashes provide technical evidence but the legal team must confirm acceptance criteria for "provable deletion" in contracts.
implementation_tasks: Extend pipeline lineage store schema to record derivation pointers for embedding and feature exports
Prototype per-day bloom-filter index generator and query library in analytics service
Implement deletion orchestrator microservice: accepts request, enumerates artifacts, creates actions plan, coordinates workers
Add audit-record writer with immutable S3 prefix and compliance DB replication
Build verification worker to compute post-action fingerprints and reconcile with audit record
Add API endpoints: POST /compliance/deletions, GET /compliance/deletions/:id/status and wire authorization to compliance role
Create Console backend API integration for Compliance UI (surface minimal metadata only)
Integration tests and chaos tests (simulate worker restarts and partial failures), end-to-end test with synthetic identity
Run security review and threat model for attack surface (s3 immutability, replay, access controls)
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): Run enumerator and audit-only mode for 2 weeks to measure coverage and false-positive rate. No destructive actions.
Phase 2 (staged destructive): Enable expire/scrub for non-critical artifacts (daily aggregates, ephemeral caches) in a staging region and process low-volume deletion requests from internal teams. Monitor verification failures.
Phase 3 (production): Enable full workflow for customer deletion requests. Expose API and Console access.
Rollback: Audit-only mode is a safe rollback; destructive actions require manual remediation plan (recompute or restore from snapshots).
testing_plan: Unit tests for bloom-filter generator and lineage queries
Integration test: end-to-end deletion for synthetic identity that touches events, embeddings, and exported CSVs
Load test: bulk process 100 concurrent deletion requests and measure median enumeration latency
Verification tests: inject deliberate mismatch to ensure verification flags requests
Compliance acceptance testing with sample legal checklist and sign-off
